widgets_values:
Exercise: calibrated stereo to 3D point cloud

Full calibrated stereo pipeline producing a colored 3D point cloud:
1. Load a stereo pair (left + right driving scene).
2. 'Stereo Calibration From CSV' reads per-image calibration:
   intrinsics K from vertical FOV, R and T from CSV columns.
3. 'cv2.stereoRectify' computes rectification transforms.
4. 'cv2.initUndistortRectifyMap' + 'cv2.remap' rectifies both views.
5. 'CV Stereo Disparity (SGBM)' computes per-pixel disparity.
6. 'CV Disparity Interpolate (Edge-Aware)' makes it dense.
7. 'cv2.reprojectImageTo3D' converts disparity to 3D points using Q.
8. The 'Sky Mask' subgraph discards the sky points.
9. 'CV Filter Point Cloud' prunes extreme-distance outliers.
10. 'CV Write PLY' exports the colored point cloud.

WHY THE INTERPOLATOR AND NOT cv2.inpaint. SGBM leaves ~40% of this
scene without a disparity (texture-less road, occlusions, the left
strip that is only visible to one camera). Filling those holes with
'cv2.inpaint' works on the ground and RUINS the objects: inpainting
is image-blind, so it diffuses disparity straight across every
silhouette - measured on this pair, only 15% of the strong disparity
gradients it produces land within 2 px of an image edge, against 85%
for the interpolator. The other tempting fix, letting the WLS filter
do the filling (see exercise_stereo_multiview), keeps the silhouettes
but bends the road: its smoothness prior is fronto-parallel, and a
plane fit through the road band degrades from 0.06 m RMS / 98%
inliers to 0.36 m / 33%. The interpolator fits a local PLANE per
superpixel instead - which is what a road IS - and keeps 0.06 m at
~100% coverage.

WHY THE SKY HAS TO BE MASKED OUT. Making the disparity dense also
fills the sky, and those points are NOT catchable downstream: they
land at a median 18 m, i.e. right inside the 0.5..50 m range filter,
and before this step they were 26% of the whole cloud (30% on frame
000001). Two things that look like they should work do not:
  - The WLS confidence map is HIGHER in the sky (mean 207) than on
    real content (163). A uniform region gives the same wrong match
    in both directions, so the left-right check is satisfied.
  - Gating the sky out of the interpolator's SEEDS makes it WORSE
    (25.7% -> 31.7% sky points): with no seeds to argue with, RIC
    extrapolates the neighbouring planes across the whole region.
    The mask has to be applied to the POINTS, which is what the
    'CV Filter Points 3D By Mask' node here does (it filters the
    per-vertex colours in lockstep).
Nor is the sky evidence-free: raw SGBM answers on 18.8% of it, so a
'only keep pixels near a seed' rule removes at most ~79% of the sky
and costs ~19% of the real content. A height cut ('keep what is
below the camera') removes 100% of it but also every building top,
tree top and lamp arm - 26% of the real content.

THE SKY MASK IS A HEURISTIC TUNED TO THIS DATASET. It is 'flat
(|Laplacian| < 2), opened, and connected to the TOP image edge',
which fits CARLA: cloudless, overexposed, noise-free, camera level,
sky always touching the top border. Expect it to fail on textured
clouds, a noisy real sensor (raise the blur, or make the threshold
a percentile), sun glare, a camera that looks down, or an indoor
scene. It covers 29% of the rectified frame here, 21% on 000001.
Four details in the composition are load-bearing:
  - the OPEN runs BEFORE the connectivity test. Without it the flat
    region leaks through the gaps between leaves, the component
    test follows the leak, and the mask swallows the tree and the
    facade behind it. Measured on the rectified frames, dropping
    the opening and relaxing the threshold to 3 marks 70% of frame
    000001 - the road included. With the opening the same threshold
    gives 21%, i.e. the result stops depending on the exact number.
  - 'Keep Largest Component' would pick the ROAD, not the sky - the
    road is flat too and, at 71344 px, larger than any single sky
    component. Touching the TOP edge is what separates them.
  - 'Select Component At Point' would not work either: the lamp
    post cuts the sky into 18 components here (13 on frame 000001),
    and one probe point catches one of them. Hence 'OpenCV
    Components Touching Border', which keeps all of them.
  - the border margin is 4 px, and it has to be. cv2.remap with
    BORDER_CONSTANT leaves a DARK SEAM one row deep at the top of a
    rectified frame (row 0 reads ~130-160 against ~220 for row 1),
    and the Gaussian + Laplacian smear that seam over another three
    rows, so the flat mask only starts answering at row 4. At
    margin 2 the sky to the right of the lamp post in frame 000001
    is never seen and half that frame's sky stays in the cloud.
    Margins 3, 4, 6 and 8 all give the identical mask, so 4 is not
    a tuned number - it is just clear of the artefact. The tempting
    wrong answer is that the OPENING ate the frame edge: it does
    not, OpenCV pads erosion with +inf so morphology never shrinks
    a region at the image border.
COLOUR SAMPLING WAS TRIED AND IS WORSE, which is worth knowing
because it is the obvious idea. Sampling the sky colour and
flood-filling from the top row (cv2.floodFill, fixed range) does
reach 100% of the sky - and also swallows the tree tops, a building
corner and the distant facades, because in this washed-out scene
everything far away is nearly the sky's colour: 18-36% of the
hand-labelled CONTENT boxes get masked, and 4-10% of the masked
pixels are strongly textured (for the shipped mask both numbers are
0.0%). A plain Lab colour-distance mask under-covers until the
tolerance is so wide it has the same problem, and growing the
confirmed sky into colour-similar neighbours (morphological
reconstruction) lands between the two. The failure mode is not the
road - mid-ground objects stop the flood before it gets there - it
is everything hazy at distance. Texture plus connectivity separates
those; colour does not.
For real footage the durable replacement is a semantic segmentation
ONNX with a sky class (Cityscapes / ADE20K) through the existing
'DNN Forward All' -> 'Pick Output' -> 'Seg Masks' pipeline: a model
file in models/onnx, no new nodes.

num_disparities is 64, not the usual 32: f*baseline is 117 px*m here,
so a 32 px search cannot see anything closer than 3.7 m - which is
exactly the ground in front of the car.

THE FAR LIMIT IS 30 m, NOT 50, and that is physics rather than
taste. Depth error grows with Z squared: with f*baseline = 117 px*m
one 1/16-px disparity step is 0.05 m at 10 m, 0.21 m at 20 m,
0.48 m at 30 m, 0.85 m at 40 m and 1.34 m at 50 m. Past ~30 m the
points cannot be better than half a metre no matter what the
matcher does. Measured against the second stereo pair (project the
cloud into that view and compare colours), cutting at 30 m drops
11% of the points and takes agreement from 74% to 77%.
Both limits are PRIMITIVE nodes on the canvas rather than widgets
on 'CV Filter Point Cloud', so the far one can be turned while
watching the 3D preview - that trade (coverage against how much
you trust the far field) is a judgement call, not a constant.

The trailing 'Flip X' is not decoration: with this calibration
stereoRectify returns a Q whose last row is negative, so
reprojectImageTo3D hands back the NEGATION of the camera frame and
the cloud would be mirrored in the viewer without it.

Dataset: StereoGeo-CARLA (CC BY 4.0, HuggingFace)
Images are 640x480 driving scenes from the CARLA simulator.

Debug: raw + interpolated disparity heatmaps, seed mask, sky mask,
3D point inspection, calibration output.
